# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs-cli` from the command tree of `osh`. Do not edit. -->

Every command of `osh` with its arguments and options, generated from the application.
The [guide](cli.md) has what a command's help does not say: how the project and the branch are
found, the output, the exit codes and the environment variables.

Every command also takes `--help`.

## `osh`

Work with Odoo.sh projects from the command line (unofficial).

```text
osh [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--version` | Show the version and exit. | |
| `--debug` | Show the traceback when a command fails. | `OSH_DEBUG` |
| `--format FORMAT` | How to print the result. One of `table`, `json`. Default: `table`. | |
| `--install-completion` | Install completion for the current shell. | |
| `--show-completion` | Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation. | |

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh auth`](#osh-auth) | Log in to Odoo.sh, log out, and show the session in use. |
| [`osh backups`](#osh-backups) | List the backups of an Odoo.sh project, take one, download one, and copy one over SSH. |
| [`osh branches`](#osh-branches) | List the branches of an Odoo.sh project, a branch's history, show and change its settings, and the revision a build runs. |
| [`osh builds`](#osh-builds) | List, show and watch the builds of a branch, start a new one, open its panels and read the mails it caught. |
| [`osh logs`](#osh-logs) | Print the end of a build's log: the install or odoo log of the branch's latest build, or another. |
| [`osh projects`](#osh-projects) | List the Odoo.sh projects you can reach, show one's overview, show and change its settings, check it, read its audit log, and list its members. |
| [`osh ssh`](#osh-ssh) | Open a shell on the branch's latest build, with your own `ssh`, its configuration and its keys. |

## `osh auth`

Log in to Odoo.sh, log out, and show the session in use.

```text
osh auth [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh auth login`](#osh-auth-login) | Sign in with GitHub in a browser and store the session in the keyring. |
| [`osh auth status`](#osh-auth-status) | Show where the session comes from and how long it lasts, without asking Odoo.sh. Exits 3 when there is none. |
| [`osh auth logout`](#osh-auth-logout) | End the stored session on Odoo.sh and remove it from the keyring. Exits 0 when there is none. |

### `osh auth login`

Sign in with GitHub in a browser and store the session in the keyring.

Where no browser can be launched, it asks for the `session_id` cookie in a prompt that does not echo it.

```text
osh auth login [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
osh auth login
```

### `osh auth status`

Show where the session comes from and how long it lasts, without asking Odoo.sh. Exits 3 when there is none.

```text
osh auth status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | Ask Odoo.sh whether it still accepts the session, and who it belongs to. | |

Example:

```bash
osh auth status --check
```

### `osh auth logout`

End the stored session on Odoo.sh and remove it from the keyring. Exits 0 when there is none.

```text
osh auth logout [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
osh auth logout
```

## `osh backups`

List the backups of an Odoo.sh project, take one, download one, and copy one over SSH.

```text
osh backups [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh backups list`](#osh-backups-list) | List a project's backups on every branch, newest first, with the time that names each one, in UTC. |
| [`osh backups create`](#osh-backups-create) | Change state on Odoo.sh: take a manual backup of a branch's latest build, which Odoo.sh keeps for 3 days. |
| [`osh backups download`](#osh-backups-download) | Change state on Odoo.sh: have it prepare a backup's file, then write it to `--output`, or print its link. |
| [`osh backups pull`](#osh-backups-pull) | Copy the daily backup of production, or a manual one, from the production build with your own `rsync` or `scp`. |

### `osh backups list`

List a project's backups on every branch, newest first, with the time that names each one, in UTC.

Odoo.sh keeps a daily backup off-site as well, under the same time: that copy is `remote`, and cannot be downloaded.

```text
osh backups list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | List only the backups taken on this branch. Default: every branch. | |

Example:

```bash
osh backups list --branch staging
```

### `osh backups create`

Change state on Odoo.sh: take a manual backup of a branch's latest build, which Odoo.sh keeps for 3 days.

Only a staging or a production branch is backed up. It asks first, unless `--yes` is given.

```text
osh backups create [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--comment COMMENT` | The comment Odoo.sh keeps with the backup, as the page's dialog asks. | |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Take the backup without asking. Needed when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |
| `--wait` | Wait until Odoo.sh has listed and finished the backup, which takes about a minute, and show it. | |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | The longest to wait for the backup to be listed. Goes with `--wait` only. At least 1. Default: `600`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh backups create --branch staging --wait
```

### `osh backups download`

Change state on Odoo.sh: have it prepare a backup's file, then write it to `--output`, or print its link.

The file is a zip of the database, neutralized unless `--exact` is given, and of its filestore unless
`--no-filestore` is. It is customer data: it is written readable by its owner alone, and deleting it is yours to do.
It asks first, unless `--yes` is given.

```text
osh backups download [OPTIONS] [BACKUP]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[BACKUP]` | The time that names the backup, in UTC, as `osh backups list` shows it, or `latest`: the newest that can be downloaded. Default: latest. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--output PATH`, `-o PATH` | The file to write, which must not exist yet. Needed unless `--link` is given. | |
| `--link` | Print the page's link to the prepared file instead of downloading it. It opens only in a browser signed in to Odoo.sh. | |
| `--exact` | The exact database, rather than the neutralized one the page offers first. | |
| `--no-filestore` | Leave the filestore out of the file. | |
| `--new` | Take a backup of the branch's latest build first, and download that one. | |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Change state without asking. Needed when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | The longest to wait for the backup, with `--new`, and for the file, each. At least 1. Default: `600`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh backups download --branch staging --output staging.zip
```

### `osh backups pull`

Copy the daily backup of production, or a manual one, from the production build with your own `rsync` or `scp`.

The file is the database's SQL, gzipped, without the filestore. It is customer data: it is written readable by its
owner alone, and deleting it is yours to do. When `ssh` does not get in, it changes state on Odoo.sh as `osh ssh`
does: it asks to allow this machine's address, unless declined.

```text
osh backups pull [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The production branch, whose build holds the backups: any other is refused. Default: the project's production branch, whatever is checked out. | |
| `--manual TIMESTAMP` | Copy the manual backup taken at this time, in UTC, as `osh backups list` shows it, on any branch, rather than the daily one. | |
| `--output PATH`, `-o PATH` | The file to write, which must not exist yet. | |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Allow this machine's address without asking, when `ssh` does not get in. Needed then when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |

Example:

```bash
osh backups pull --output daily.sql.gz
```

## `osh branches`

List the branches of an Odoo.sh project, a branch's history, show and change its settings, and the revision a build runs.

```text
osh branches [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh branches list`](#osh-branches-list) | List a project's branches with their stage: production, staging, then development, each sorted by name. |
| [`osh branches history`](#osh-branches-history) | List a branch's history, newest first: each push with its commits, each rebuild and each move between stages. |
| [`osh branches revision`](#osh-branches-revision) | Show what a build of a branch runs: its head commit, its Odoo version, and the Odoo revision the branch has selected. The latest build, or `--build`. |
| [`osh branches settings`](#osh-branches-settings) | Show a branch's settings, or change them. |

### `osh branches list`

List a project's branches with their stage: production, staging, then development, each sorted by name.

A stage `osh` does not know is shown as Odoo.sh names it, after the others. In the table, `*` marks the branch checked out, when the project comes from the git checkout.

```text
osh branches list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--stage STAGE` | List only the branches in this stage. Can be given more than once. `unknown` is any stage `osh` does not know. One of `production`, `staging`, `development`, `unknown`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh branches list --stage staging
```

### `osh branches history`

List a branch's history, newest first: each push with its commits, each rebuild and each move between stages.

A push lists each commit by its short hash and the first line of its message, and `--commits` prints them in full. The build is the one the event made, as it is now: `osh builds show` has the rest of it.

```text
osh branches history [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--limit LIMIT` | The most events to list, 200 at most. From 1 to 200. Default: `10`. | |
| `--commits` | Print each commit in full: its whole hash, its address and its whole message. | |

Example:

```bash
osh branches history --branch staging --limit 30
```

### `osh branches revision`

Show what a build of a branch runs: its head commit, its Odoo version, and the Odoo revision the branch has selected. The latest build, or `--build`.

Odoo.sh ties no Odoo revision to a build: the branch's is the one it has selected now, which the build may not run. Odoo.sh gives no commit for a submodule, and a line on stderr says so.

```text
osh branches revision [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--build BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the latest one. At least 1. | |

Example:

```bash
osh branches revision --branch staging
```

### `osh branches settings`

Show a branch's settings, or change them.

```text
osh branches settings [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh branches settings show`](#osh-branches-settings-show) | Show a branch's settings, one per line, as its Settings tab has them. |
| [`osh branches settings set`](#osh-branches-settings-set) | Change state on Odoo.sh: change a branch's settings, sending only those given. |

#### `osh branches settings show`

Show a branch's settings, one per line, as its Settings tab has them.

The new build options, from `Project defaults` to `AI agent`, apply to a development branch only, and not while it uses the project's defaults.

```text
osh branches settings show [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |

Example:

```bash
osh branches settings show --branch staging
```

#### `osh branches settings set`

Change state on Odoo.sh: change a branch's settings, sending only those given.

The others keep their value. NAME is one of push_behavior, project_defaults, module_install, modules, tests, test_tags, demo_data and ai_agent. A choice takes a value `show --format json` prints, a yes or no takes `yes` or `no`, `modules` takes names separated by commas, and `test_tags=` clears the tags. Only a development branch has new build options, and while the project's defaults apply they are changed with `project_defaults=no` too. What a new commit does is not changed on a production branch. It asks first, unless `--yes` is given.

```text
osh branches settings set [OPTIONS] {NAME=VALUE...}
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NAME=VALUE...` | A setting and its new value, named as `osh branches settings show --format json` prints them. Required. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Change without asking. Needed when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |

Example:

```bash
osh branches settings set --branch feature-x ai_agent=opencode
```

## `osh builds`

List, show and watch the builds of a branch, start a new one, open its panels and read the mails it caught.

```text
osh builds [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh builds list`](#osh-builds-list) | List a branch's latest builds, newest first, with their status, result and commit. |
| [`osh builds show`](#osh-builds-show) | Show one build of a branch, with its commit and the address of its database: its latest, or BUILD_ID. |
| [`osh builds watch`](#osh-builds-watch) | Watch a build until it finishes, and exit with its result: the build of HEAD, or BUILD_ID. |
| [`osh builds rebuild`](#osh-builds-rebuild) | Change state on Odoo.sh: start a new build of a branch, which replaces its latest one. |
| [`osh builds open`](#osh-builds-open) | Print the URL of a build's monitor, shell or editor: of its latest build, or BUILD_ID. |
| [`osh builds mails`](#osh-builds-mails) | List the mails a build of a development or a staging branch caught: of its latest build, or BUILD_ID. |

### `osh builds list`

List a branch's latest builds, newest first, with their status, result and commit.

```text
osh builds list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--limit LIMIT` | The most builds to list. Odoo.sh has only been seen to answer up to 4: older builds are out of reach. At least 1. Default: `4`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh builds list --branch staging
```

### `osh builds show`

Show one build of a branch, with its commit and the address of its database: its latest, or BUILD_ID.

```text
osh builds show [OPTIONS] [BUILD_ID]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the latest one. At least 1. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |

Example:

```bash
osh builds show 1234
```

### `osh builds watch`

Watch a build until it finishes, and exit with its result: the build of HEAD, or BUILD_ID.

```text
osh builds watch [OPTIONS] [BUILD_ID]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the build of HEAD when the project and the branch are the checkout's, the latest build otherwise. At least 1. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | The longest to wait for the build to appear and to finish. At least 1. Default: `1800`. | |
| `--commit SHA` | Wait for a build of this commit, given as the first 7 to 64 digits of its hash. Default: the git checkout's HEAD, when the project and the branch are the checkout's. Goes with neither BUILD_ID nor `--no-wait`. | |
| `--no-wait` | Watch the branch's latest build, whatever its commit. | |

Example:

```bash
git push && osh builds watch
```

### `osh builds rebuild`

Change state on Odoo.sh: start a new build of a branch, which replaces its latest one.

Only a development or a staging branch is rebuilt. It asks first, unless `--yes` is given.

```text
osh builds rebuild [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Rebuild without asking. Needed when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |
| `--watch` | Watch the new build until it finishes, and exit with its result. | |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | The longest to wait for the new build to finish. Goes with `--watch` only. At least 1. Default: `1800`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh builds rebuild --watch
```

### `osh builds open`

Print the URL of a build's monitor, shell or editor: of its latest build, or BUILD_ID.

The monitor is the branch's, for a staging or a production branch, and takes no BUILD_ID.

```text
osh builds open [OPTIONS] {PANEL} [BUILD_ID]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `PANEL` | The panel: the branch's monitor, or the shell or the editor on the build's own host. Required. One of `monitor`, `shell`, `editor`. |
| `BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the latest one. At least 1. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--open` | Open the panel in your default browser rather than print its URL. The browser signs in to Odoo.sh on its own. | |

Example:

```bash
osh builds open shell --open
```

### `osh builds mails`

List the mails a build of a development or a staging branch caught: of its latest build, or BUILD_ID.

Odoo.sh catches them rather than sending them. `--mail` shows one with its body. Their text is
the build's: it is printed without escape sequences or control characters.

```text
osh builds mails [OPTIONS] [BUILD_ID]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the latest one. At least 1. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--mail MAIL_ID` | Show this mail with its body, rather than list. | |
| `--limit LIMIT` | The most mails to list, newest first. Goes without `--mail`. At least 1. Default: `20`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh builds mails --branch staging
```

## `osh logs`

Print the end of a build's log: the install or odoo log of the branch's latest build, or another.

```text
osh logs [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--build BUILD_ID` | The build's number, among the branch's latest builds. Default: the latest one. At least 1. | |
| `--kind NAME` | Which log to print, by its name. `--kinds` lists them. Default: `install` when the build has it, `odoo` otherwise. | |
| `--kinds` | List the logs the build has, and print none. Goes with none of the options that print a log. | |
| `--tail LINES` | Print the last lines, out of the log's last mebibyte: a large tail can print fewer. At least 1. Default: `100`. | |
| `--all` | Print the whole log. Does not go with `--tail`. | |
| `--follow`, `-f` | Keep printing the lines as they are written, until interrupted. With `--all`, from the first line. | |
| `--strip`, `--no-strip` | Remove the escape sequences and control characters from the lines, or leave them. Default: remove them when stdout is a terminal. | |
| `--timeout SECONDS` | The longest to follow the log: the command then exits 8. Goes with `--follow` only. Default: no limit. At least 1. | |

Example:

```bash
osh logs --follow
```

## `osh projects`

List the Odoo.sh projects you can reach, show one's overview, show and change its settings, check it, read its audit log, and list its members.

```text
osh projects [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh projects list`](#osh-projects-list) | List the projects you can reach, with their repository and address. |
| [`osh projects show`](#osh-projects-show) | Show a project's overview, one fact per line: its subscription, Odoo version, hosting, production build and branches by stage. |
| [`osh projects audit`](#osh-projects-audit) | List a project's audit log, newest first: who did what, when, on which stage, and what Odoo.sh adds about it. |
| [`osh projects members`](#osh-projects-members) | List a project's members with their role, highest role first, then by login. |
| [`osh projects check`](#osh-projects-check) | Check a project's subscription, production build, storage and branches, and exit 30 when one fails, 31 when one warns. |
| [`osh projects settings`](#osh-projects-settings) | Show a project's settings, or change them. |

### `osh projects list`

List the projects you can reach, with their repository and address.

```text
osh projects list [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
osh projects list
```

### `osh projects show`

Show a project's overview, one fact per line: its subscription, Odoo version, hosting, production build and branches by stage.

Storage, workers and staging branches are on the project's Settings page, which Odoo.sh shows to an admin of the project only: anyone else gets `admins only`.

```text
osh projects show [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |

Example:

```bash
osh projects show --project acme-shop
```

### `osh projects audit`

List a project's audit log, newest first: who did what, when, on which stage, and what Odoo.sh adds about it.

Odoo.sh sends the last 30 days in one answer, and shows the log to an admin of the project only: anyone else gets exit code 5. Nothing older than 30 days can be read, whatever `--since` says.

```text
osh projects audit [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--limit LIMIT` | The most entries to list, 200 at most. From 1 to 200. Default: `20`. | |
| `--since DATE` | List only the entries at or after this moment, in UTC, such as 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-01T09:30:00. | |

Example:

```bash
osh projects audit --limit 10
```

### `osh projects members`

List a project's members with their role, highest role first, then by login.

Odoo.sh lists them to an admin of the project only: anyone else gets exit code 5. `Logged in` is `no` for a member invited who has not logged in to Odoo.sh yet. It changes nothing.

```text
osh projects members [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |

Example:

```bash
osh projects members --project acme-shop
```

### `osh projects check`

Check a project's subscription, production build, storage and branches, and exit 30 when one fails, 31 when one warns.

Each check is a row: its name, `pass`, `warn`, `fail` or `skip`, and the fact it was judged on. Storage is on the project's Settings page, which Odoo.sh shows to an admin of the project only: anyone else gets `skip`, which does not count in the exit code.

```text
osh projects check [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--storage-margin PERCENT` | Warn when the storage used is within this share of the quota. 0 never warns, 100 warns on any use. From 0 to 100. Default: `10`. | |

Example:

```bash
osh projects check --project acme-shop
```

### `osh projects settings`

Show a project's settings, or change them.

```text
osh projects settings [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`osh projects settings show`](#osh-projects-settings-show) | Show a project's settings, one per line, as its Settings page has them. |
| [`osh projects settings set`](#osh-projects-settings-set) | Change state on Odoo.sh: change a project's settings, sending only those given. |

#### `osh projects settings show`

Show a project's settings, one per line, as its Settings page has them.

Odoo.sh shows them to an admin of the project only: anyone else gets exit code 5. The rows from `Dev install` to `Dev AI agent` are the defaults of new development branches. A submodule's public deploy key is in `--format json` only.

```text
osh projects settings show [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |

Example:

```bash
osh projects settings show --project acme-shop
```

#### `osh projects settings set`

Change state on Odoo.sh: change a project's settings, sending only those given.

The others keep their value. NAME is one of session_lifetime, public, http_timeout_seconds, cron_timeout_seconds, module_install, modules, tests, test_tags, demo_data and ai_agent, the last six being the defaults of new development branches. A choice takes a value `show --format json` prints, a yes or no takes `yes` or `no`, a timeout takes seconds, a multiple of 60, and is changed on a dedicated server only, `modules` takes names separated by commas, and `test_tags=` clears the tags. The IP allow list, which SSH and PostgreSQL to production and staging go through, is changed by entry with `--add-ip` and `--remove-ip`, ten entries at most. Only an admin of the project can change them: anyone else gets exit code 5. It asks first, saying when the change is to who can reach the project, unless `--yes` is given.

```text
osh projects settings set [OPTIONS] [NAME=VALUE]...
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[NAME=VALUE]...` | A setting and its new value, named as `osh projects settings show --format json` prints them. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--add-ip IP` | An IPv4 address to add to the IP allow list. Can be given more than once. | |
| `--remove-ip ENTRY` | An address or a network to remove from the IP allow list, as `osh projects settings show` lists it. Can be given more than once. | |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Change without asking. Needed when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |

Example:

```bash
osh projects settings set --project acme-shop --add-ip 203.0.113.7
```

## `osh ssh`

Open a shell on the branch's latest build, with your own `ssh`, its configuration and its keys.

It first tries `ssh` with no prompt. When that does not get in, it changes state on Odoo.sh: it
asks Odoo.sh to allow this machine's address for one hour, unless declined, and tries again
for up to ten minutes.

```text
osh ssh [OPTIONS] [SSH_ARGS]...
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[SSH_ARGS]...` | What to give `ssh` after the host: its own options, or a command to run on the build. Everything from the first one on is `ssh`'s. Put `--` before it when it starts with a dash. |

| Option | Description | Environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--project PROJECT` | The project's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_PROJECT` |
| `--branch BRANCH` | The branch's name. Default: the git checkout's. | `OSH_BRANCH` |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Allow this machine's address without asking, when `ssh` does not get in. Needed then when stdin or stderr is not a terminal. | |

Example:

```bash
osh ssh --branch staging -- ls
```
